about: Two community tradeskill guides as data. Written by scripts/community/guides-pull.mts at release time; never edited by hand. Each guide is its author's work: show the title, the author and the link wherever its data is shown.

leveling.title: EQ Legends Tradeskill Guide
leveling.author: Zakarsis Moonstalker - Iksar Monk / Druid / Enchanter

overview.heading: Notes
lines: Alchemy is no longer shaman only.  Everyone can learn it.
Tinkering is still gnome only.  You must unlock the gnome race to learn it.
Spell Research was removed from EQ Legends.
Plan ahead for the tradeskill(s) you wish to max.  Once you pass 200 in any one skill, all other tradeskills will cap out at 200
With each rank of the AA Crafting Mastery you can raise an additional tradeskill to 300

overview.heading: Stats
lines: Charisma affects your buying/selling prices with merchants.
Chance of skill increase is based on the highest of your int/wis with 2 exceptions
Illusions and sneak can also help with merchant prices, and getting into KOS areas.
For the above reasons I recommend having an enchanter in your trio to do tradeskills.

notes: Recommend getting a Reinforced Medicine Bag before starting.

notes: For jewelcrafting I chose to make things closer to the trivial.  That gives a better chance to make the item, thus selling it back to recoup the costs.
Ruby is the highest gem available on merchants.  It is recommended to save all black sapphires, jacinth, diamonds, and blue diamonds for 280+
All trivials and combines assume enchanted bars.  Non-enchanted bar trivials are lower.  Champagne Magnum requires an enchanted bar.
Best place for spider silk:  Sol B lava duct crawler area.  Lguk just past the bedroom.  EK near the ramp to highhold
Best place for spiderling silk:  Feerott near the druid ring.  Gukta (rathe mtns).

notes: Creating a gnome or unlocking gnome race (and using it in your loadout) will automatically give you a skill of 50 in tinkering

Recommend not doing this skill until level 50.  There is a level-based skill cap on tinkering.  At level 14 I was unable to get a skillup in 200 combines (at 50 skill).  Upon swapping to a level 50 loadout, skillups were normal
Leveling tinkering is INCREDIBLY expensive per combine.  Unlike jewelcrafting, selling what you make doesn't yield close to what you spend.
Aqualung clocks in at about 210pp per combine.  Nantik's anti-gravity unit at 360pp, and rebreather(if you choose to make it) at a whopping 892pp per combine
While footwarming boots ARE cheaper to make, the leather padding (and smithing skill) are a huge bottleneck.  Feel free to choose your own upgrade path based on the below suggestions
